slides.teacher_cue: Two common endings. -nge = /ndʒ/: change, strange, range, plunge, fringe. The g is soft because it is before e — so -nge = n + soft g = /ndʒ/. -nce = /ns/: dance, fence, since, prince, bounce, chance. The c is soft because it is before e — so -nce = n + soft c = /ns/. Both patterns use the soft letter rule you already know.
slides.expected_response: Students apply the soft letter rule to read -nge and -nce endings correctly.
slides.correction_move: Show: -nge = n + /dʒ/ (soft g before e). -nce = n + /s/ (soft c before e). Students connect these endings to the soft c/g rule from Lesson 41.
slides.observation_note: Watch for hard /g/ in -nge (producing /ng/ instead of /ndʒ/) and hard /k/ in -nce.

slides.observation_note: Listen for whether students can carry the focus from isolation into a real word.
